subject: microbiology
title: Clostridia, non-sporing anaerobes and actinomycetes

steps.tx: Clostridia are **Gram-positive, spore-forming, obligate anaerobes**. Most are motile, but **Clostridium perfringens** and one tetanus type are non-motile. The big exam toxin-producers are C. perfringens, C. tetani, and C. botulinum. Learn each organism by its disease and its toxin, because the same toxin family can act in opposite ways.
steps.say: Clostridia are Gram-positive, spore-forming, obligate anaerobes. Most are motile, but Clostridium perfringens is non-motile. The important toxin-producers for exams are Clostridium perfringens, Clostridium tetani, and Clostridium botulinum. Learn each organism by its disease and its toxin, because similar toxin families can act in opposite ways.

steps.tx: **Clostridium tetani** is a Gram-positive rod with **terminal spores** that give a drumstick appearance. It is an obligate anaerobe. Tetanospasmin is plasmid-coded and blocks release of GABA and glycine at presynaptic terminals. This causes spastic paralysis. Botulinum toxin, by contrast, blocks acetylcholine release and causes flaccid paralysis.

right.title: Botulism (botulinum toxin)
points: Ingested toxin in food or honey

steps.tx: **Botulism** causes symmetric descending flaccid paralysis, starting with diplopia, dysarthria and dysphagia. **Infant botulism** gives floppiness and constipation, and honey is the classic food link. The toxin is produced inside the organism and released on death and autolysis, and it is heat labile. Bacteroides fragilis is a frequent anaerobe whose LPS is much less potent than endotoxin, so shock is unusual.
steps.say: Botulism causes symmetric descending flaccid paralysis, starting with diplopia, dysarthria and dysphagia. Infant botulism gives floppiness and constipation, and honey is the classic food link. The toxin is heat labile, though spores are very heat resistant. Bacteroides fragilis is a common anaerobe whose lipopolysaccharide is much less potent than endotoxin, so shock is unusual.

steps.tx: **Actinomyces israelii** is an anaerobic, Gram-positive, non-acid-fast filamentous organism that forms part of the gingival flora. It causes **cervicofacial actinomycosis**, the commonest form, along with thoracic, abdominal and pelvic forms. Sulphur granules in pus and branching filaments on smear are key clues. Penicillin is the drug of choice, given for months. **Nocardia** is aerobic, weakly Gram-positive and modified acid-fast, and causes pulmonary disease and brain abscess. Actinomycetoma is caused by Actinomyces or Nocardia, not fungi.
steps.say: Actinomyces israelii is an anaerobic, Gram-positive, non-acid-fast filamentous organism from the gingival flora. It causes cervicofacial actinomycosis, the commonest form, along with thoracic, abdominal and pelvic forms. Sulphur granules in pus and branching filaments on smear are key clues. Penicillin is the drug of choice, given for months. Nocardia is aerobic and modified acid-fast, causing pulmonary disease and brain abscess.

steps.tx: Remember the **Robertson cooked meat medium**, used to grow clostridia, and the **sulphur granule** clue for actinomycetes. Mycetoma from Actinomyces or Nocardia shows grains, while eumycotic mycetoma shows fungal hyphae. The exam trap is that actinomycetes are bacteria, not fungi, though they look like fungi. Clostridium difficile causes antibiotic-associated colitis and is discussed under its own toxins.
